The '''2022–23 Serie A''' (known as the '''Serie A [[Telecom Italia|TIM]]''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 121st season of top-tier Italian [[association football|football]], the 91st in a [[round-robin tournament]], and the 13th since its organization under an own league committee, the [[Lega Serie A]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lega Serie A|url=https://www.legaseriea.it/en|website=Serie A official website|access-date=5 March 2022|archive-date=10 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210410234319/https://www.legaseriea.it/en|url-status=live}}</ref> [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]] won the title with five matches remaining after a 1–1 draw against [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]] at the [[Dacia Arena]] on 4 May 2023.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.legaseriea.it/en/media/serie-a/napoli-are-champions-of-italy-6m91mha|title=Napoli are champions of Italy|publisher=Serie A|date= 4 May 2023|access-date=4 May 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Rindl|url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65488842|title=Udinese 1–1 Napoli: Southern Italian team wins Serie A title for first time in 33 years|date=4 May 2023|work=BBC Sport|access-date=5 May 2023}}</ref>

Napoli's title was their third league title in club history and their first since [[Diego Maradona]] led them to victory in [[1989–90 Serie A|1990]] — bringing an end to their 33-year ''[[Scudetto]]'' drought. [[AC Milan]], the defending champions, finished in fourth place. It was the first time since [[AS Roma|Roma]] in [[2000-01 Serie A|2001]] that a club other than AC Milan, [[Inter Milan]] or [[Juventus]] had won the Serie A title.

==Summary==
This year would mark the return of playoff matches for the first time since [[2004–05 Serie A|2005]]. If the season ends with two teams tied at the top of the league standings, those teams would play at a neutral site to determine the title winner. The match will have no [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]], and will instead go directly to a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] should the teams be tied after regulation. Head-to-head will still will used as a tiebreaker elsewhere on the board.<ref>{{cite news |date=29 June 2022 |title=Serie A to decide title by playoff in case of tie |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/italian-serie-a/story/4692513/serie-a-will-decide-scudetto-winner-by-playoff-in-case-of-tie-in-the-table |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220629233001/https://www.espn.com/soccer/italian-serie-a/story/4692513/serie-a-will-decide-scudetto-winner-by-playoff-in-case-of-tie-in-the-table |archive-date=29 June 2022 |access-date=30 June 2022 |work=ESPN |language=en |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

The [[Lega Serie A]] in February announced their intention to run a tournament in the [[United States]] during the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]], consisting of players who were not called up to play for the [[Italy national football team|men's national team]]. The unusual scheduling of the World Cup in [[Qatar]] forced many leagues to interrupt their seasons for weeks, so the Serie A saw this as an opportunity to bolster its image abroad while keeping its players active.<ref>{{cite news |title=Serie A plans U.S. tournament during World Cup |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/italian-serie-a/story/4596225/serie-a-planning-us-tournament-during-world-cup-chief-executive-luigi-de-siervo |access-date=30 June 2022 |work=ESPN |agency=Reuters |date=18 February 2022 |language=en |archive-date=30 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220630111706/https://www.espn.com/soccer/italian-serie-a/story/4596225/serie-a-planning-us-tournament-during-world-cup-chief-executive-luigi-de-siervo |url-status=live }}</ref> The idea received mixed feedback, and was ultimately cancelled by the league due to logistical and funding issues.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://football-italia.net/plans-for-serie-a-tournament-in-usa-cancelled/|title=Plans for Serie A tournament in USA cancelled|last=Heyes|first=Apollo|date=20 May 2022|work=Football Italia|access-date=3 January 2023|archive-date=3 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230103042621/https://football-italia.net/plans-for-serie-a-tournament-in-usa-cancelled/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In January 2023, the Serie A deducted 15 points from [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] after an investigation by the [[Italian Football Federation|FIGC]] accused the club of manipulating their balancing sheets to show false gains of around 60m euros. Months later in April, Italy's highest court ordered the case to be re-examined, and the points were restored. The original ruling was upheld—though this time resulting in Juventus being docked 10 points—in May 2023.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65677783 |title=Juventus docked 10 points in Serie A at new hearing into transfer dealings |publisher=BBC Sport |date=22 May 2023 |access-date=22 May 2023}}</ref>

On 28 July 2023, [[UEFA]] released a statement confirming Juventus has violated finance regulations.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2023-07-28 |title=The CFCB concludes its proceedings against Juventus and Chelsea FC |url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/0283-1899ede31dd4-3e4a12d922fd-1000--the-cfcb-concludes-its-proceedings-against-juventus-and-/ |access-date=2023-07-28 |website=UEFA |language=en}}</ref> Consequently, Juventus faced penalties including exclusion from the [[2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Juventus kicked out of Europe by Uefa |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66342566 |access-date=2023-07-28}}</ref>

== Teams ==
[[US Cremonese|Cremonese]] returned to the [[Serie A]] for the first time in 26 years—their longest absence from the top league in history. [[US Lecce|Lecce]] returned after two years. [[AC Monza|Monza]] were promoted for the first time in the club's history, making them the 67th team to play at the highest level of Italian football.

[[Cagliari Calcio|Cagliari]] were relegated to the [[Serie B]] after six years, while [[Venezia FC|Venezia]] were relegated after only one. [[Genoa C.F.C.|Genoa]] were relegated after 15 seasons, thus ending the club's longest consecutive run in the top league.

This was the first season since the [[2003–04 Serie A|2003–04 campaign]] without any representation from the [[archipelago]]s of Italy (teams located on [[Sardinia]] or [[Sicily]]) in the Serie A.

==Relegation tie-breaker==
As [[Spezia Calcio|Spezia]] and [[Hellas Verona F.C.|Hellas Verona]] finished level on points in the final relegation spot, a one-match relegation tie-breaker was held at a neutral venue to determine the final team which would be relegated to [[2023–24 Serie B|Serie B]].
{{football box
|date = 11 June 2023
|time = 20:45 [[UTC+2|CEST]]
|team1 = [[Spezia Calcio|Spezia]]
|score = 1–3
|report = https://www.legaseriea.it/en/match/2022-23aspareuni1spever
|team2 = [[Hellas Verona F.C.|Hellas Verona]]
|goals1 = 
*[[Ethan Ampadu|Ampadu]] {{goal|15}}
|goals2 = 
*[[Davide Faraoni|Faraoni]] {{goal|5}}
*[[Cyril Ngonge|Ngonge]] {{goal|26||38}}
|stadium = [[Mapei Stadium – Città del Tricolore]], [[Reggio Emilia]]
|attendance = 15,000
|referee = [[Daniele Orsato]]
}}
''Hellas Verona won 3–1 and remained in [[2023-24 Serie A|Serie A]], while Spezia were relegated to [[2023–24 Serie B|Serie B]].''
